# Discussion: Functions as first-class objects

Notes from a design discussion about `AbstractMapping{DT,CT,D}` in
`src/mathematics/mappings.jl`. Question: does a Julia package already exist
that treats functions as first-class mathematical objects (typed
domain/codomain, algebra, composition, differentiation)? Result: no single
package covers this; the need keeps getting solved per-domain. Below are the
closest matches found.

## Closest structural match: `AbstractAlgebra.jl` Map interface

<https://nemocas.github.io/AbstractAlgebra.jl/stable/map_interface/>

Part of the Nemo computer-algebra ecosystem. Maps are objects distinct from
plain Julia functions:

```
Map{D, C, T, MyMap}
```

- `D`, `C` — domain and codomain
- `T` — map class (e.g. `SetMap`, `FunctionalMap`)
- `MyMap` — concrete implementation

Interface: `domain(M)`, `codomain(M)` as accessor **methods**, `M(a)` for
application, `compose(f, g)` / `*` for composition, an `IdentityMap` type.

Relevant to the `D` (restricted-domain) parameter question: domain/codomain
here are returned by methods, not encoded as a value baked into the type.
Independent precedent for dropping the domain-restriction type parameter in
favor of a `domain(m)` method with a fallback derived from `DT`.

## Linear and general operators

- **LinearMaps.jl** — <https://github.com/JuliaLinearAlgebra/LinearMaps.jl>
  Wraps a function as a lazy linear operator (`LinearMap(f, n)`). Supports
  `+`, `*`, adjoint/transpose, composition, Kronecker products,
  concatenation — never materializes a matrix. Standard operator interface
  behind IterativeSolvers.jl / Krylov.jl. Likely the "general linear algebra
  package" referenced from memory in the discussion.
- **AbstractOperators.jl** — <https://github.com/kul-optec/AbstractOperators.jl>
  Same idea generalized to nonlinear operators, arbitrary-dimension
  domains/codomains. Built for large-scale optimization.
- **FunctionOperators.jl** — <https://juliapackages.com/p/functionoperators>
  Same spirit, used in MRI image reconstruction.

## Geometric transformations

- **CoordinateTransformations.jl** —
  <https://github.com/JuliaGeometry/CoordinateTransformations.jl>
  `Translation`, `LinearMap`, `AffineMap` as composable, invertible objects
  (`trans ∘ rot`, `inv(t)`). Used throughout the JuliaGeometry/Makie stack.
- Makie itself has no function-object type; it leans on **IntervalSets.jl**'s
  `..` to pass a domain alongside a plain function, e.g.
  `surface!(ga, lonmin..lonmax, latmin..latmax, field)`. MMJMesh already
  depends on IntervalSets.jl for the same pattern.

## Domain algebra

- **DomainSets.jl** — <https://github.com/JuliaApproximation/DomainSets.jl>
  (already an MMJMesh dependency). Abstract `Domain{T}` with
  union/intersect/product/membership, plus its own minimal internal `Map`
  for domain transformations.

## Numeric / approximate function algebra

- **ApproxFun.jl** — functions represented via basis expansion
  (Chebyshev/Fourier), full algebra (`+`, `*`, `'`, `∫`), domain-aware via
  DomainSets.jl. Works to ~machine precision, not exact. The community's
  standard answer when this question comes up (see Discourse thread below).
- **TaylorSeries.jl** — <https://github.com/JuliaDiff/TaylorSeries.jl>
  Full algebra (`+`, `*`, `/`, composition, `derivative`, `integrate`,
  elementary functions) on truncated power series (`Taylor1`,
  `HomogeneousPolynomial`, `TaylorN`). Mature, successfully adopted
  (TaylorIntegration.jl, TaylorModels.jl). Evidence that "functions as
  objects, done well" is achievable once the representation is narrowed
  (here: local polynomial expansion) rather than fully general.

## Prior community discussion

["Package for mathematical functions?"](https://discourse.julialang.org/t/package-for-mathematical-functions/32861)
— Julia Discourse, ~2019. Same question asked before. Chris Rackauckas
points to ApproxFun.jl; someone prototypes on AbstractAlgebra.jl's `Map` and
calls it "a little unwieldy"; Lazy.jl comes up as the fallback for
exact-but-unstructured closures. No answer covers
domain-awareness + exactness + generality together.

## Takeaway

No package combines: typed domain/codomain, exact (not floating-point
approximate) algebra, and general (not linear-only, not local-expansion-only)
function representation. `MPolynomial` and `AbstractMapping` in MMJMesh sit
in the gap on purpose, scoped to what FE basis construction needs — same
conclusion as `DynamicPolynomials.jl`/`MultivariatePolynomials.jl` occupying
the "real polynomial type" gap that `Symbolics.jl` leaves open (see
`mpolynomials.jl`).
